body:
hey there - 

not sure what's different in your test but I can't reproduce this in a simple setup:
```py

from sqlalchemy.sql.functions import FunctionElement
from sqlalchemy.ext.compiler import compiles
from sqlalchemy import column, select, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql

class now(FunctionElement):
    name = "now"



@compiles(now)
def compile(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    raise NotImplementedError("last is only defined for postgresql")


@compiles(now, "postgresql")
def compile_postgres(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    return "current_timestamp"


def go(engine):
    stmt = select(now())

    with engine.connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(stmt).scalar()


engine = create_engine("postgresql://scott:tiger@localhost/test", echo=True)
go(engine)

go(engine)
```

it's also unclear what the failure mode you are seeing is, you say " there is no explicit error message, rather the wrong specification is picked up by the runtime for different dialects", your code seems to have only the PostgreSQL dialect defined.    Are there other implementations for other backends that don't raise notimplemented?   What is the SQL output you are seeing?       Does it include any verbiage about caching?  The functionelement you have does not have caching indicators so the log output should indicate "No Key".

if you can construct a self contained [MCVE](http://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve) that would be helpful.

this is an old issue that comes around from time to time, and I did actually fix something here very recently in 1.4 related to this so im not sure how it's surfaced again.  if you look in the stack trace, there's a naive str() being called:

```
File "/home/classic/dev/sqlalchemy/lib/sqlalchemy/util/langhelpers.py", line 1093, in __get__
    obj.__dict__[self.__name__] = result = self.fget(obj)
  File "/home/classic/dev/sqlalchemy/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py", line 907, in _proxy_key
    return str(self)
  File "/home/classic/dev/sqlalchemy/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py", line 574, in __str__
    return str(self.compile())

```
I'll look up the issue I fixed in 1.4 with a similar problem.   anyway the workaround is simple, give your function a label so that it doesnt' have to invent a key:

```
        subq = session.query(
            now().label(),
        ).subquery()


```
thanks for taking the time to create a great test case!

this condition can be reproduced in 1.3 as well like this, so this is not new, it's just the ORM is working in a more "core-like" way now so we see it in more places:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
from sqlalchemy.ext.compiler import compiles
from sqlalchemy.sql.functions import FunctionElement


class now(FunctionElement):
    name = "now"


@compiles(now)
def compile(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    raise NotImplementedError(f"this function is only defined for postgresql")


@compiles(now, "postgresql")
def compile_postgres(element, compiler, **kwargs):
    return "current_timestamp"

subq = select([now()]).alias()

stmt = select([subq])

print(stmt.compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect()))

```

```

awesome, thanks so much @zzzeek - and yes I figured it was that "naked" call to compile() from the str() as well. thanks for the workaround

issue.title: Compatability with SQLAlchemy 1.4.x ,  Remove python-dateutil version pin
issue.body:
* Unpin `python-dateutil` and remove the dependency altogether - Doesn't seem to be required anymore, and since this library is a dependency for many of our services, it is blocking us from removing this pin in many other places as well.
* Fixes a current regression that affects `sqlalchemy` 1.4.x and up to do with usage of `compiles()` and `from_self()`. See more information [here](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6256)

body: I'm going to take another crack at getting rid of that str() call.  it just shouldnt be there.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:
